findings.body: The invalid `-ms-align-items` declaration is discarded, and no `-moz-box-align` declaration is emitted, so headers and small-action rows are not centered and bullet badges are not baseline-aligned in the supported fallback syntax.
findings.failure_mode: The old Mozilla flexbox fallback uses its default cross-axis alignment rather than the requested alignment.
findings.impact: The invalid `-ms-align-items` declaration is discarded, and no `-moz-box-align` declaration is emitted, so headers and small-action rows are not centered and bullet badges are not baseline-aligned in the supported fallback syntax.
findings.root_cause: The vendor-specific alignment declaration names the wrong vendor and a nonexistent CSS property.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace this declaration with `-moz-box-align: $alignment;`; retain the preceding valid `-ms-flex-align` declaration for Microsoft flexbox.
findings.title: The alignment mixin uses an invalid MS property instead of supporting old Mozilla flexbox
findings.trigger: Load any new flex layout in a Firefox version that selects the mixin's `display: -moz-box` fallback.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 121 verbatim shows '-ms-align-items: $alignment;' which is indeed an invalid CSS property. The correct MS flexbox property is -ms-flex-align (already on line 120). The -ms-align-items property does not exist. Additionally, the mixin lacks -moz-box-align for old Mozilla flexbox fallback. The trigger (Firefox using -moz-box fallback) is realistic for legacy browsers, and the impact (alignment not applied) follows from the invalid/missing declarations.

pr.title: Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins

raw_findings.body: `.small-action-desc` becomes a non-growing flex item sized from its content, so its `float: right` edit/delete buttons align to the edge of that narrow item instead of the 755px action row.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Edit and delete controls appear beside the description rather than at the right edge of the action row.
raw_findings.impact: `.small-action-desc` becomes a non-growing flex item sized from its content, so its `float: right` edit/delete buttons align to the edge of that narrow item instead of the 755px action row.
raw_findings.root_cause: The container was converted to flex layout without allowing the description flex item to grow.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Give `.small-action-desc` the remaining row width, for example with `flex: 1` and the required supported prefixes.
raw_findings.title: Small-action controls no longer align to the right edge
raw_findings.trigger: Render a small-action post for which the current user can edit or delete the post.

raw_findings.body: The 2009 box syntax defaults to ordinal group 1 and only accepts positive groups, whereas standard flex items default to order 0 and permit zero or negative values. The fallback therefore ties `order(1)` with unordered items or rejects nonpositive values, producing a different item order in legacy WebKit/Mozilla browsers.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The same mixin invocation produces different visual ordering depending on which flexbox syntax the browser supports.
raw_findings.impact: The 2009 box syntax defaults to ordinal group 1 and only accepts positive groups, whereas standard flex items default to order 0 and permit zero or negative values. The fallback therefore ties `order(1)` with unordered items or rejects nonpositive values, producing a different item order in legacy WebKit/Mozilla browsers.
raw_findings.root_cause: The mixin passes a zero-based standard flex order directly to the one-based legacy box ordinal API.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Emit `$val + 1` for both `*-box-ordinal-group` declarations while retaining `$val` for `-ms-flex-order`, `-webkit-order`, and standard `order`.
raw_findings.title: Legacy box ordinal values do not preserve standard `order` semantics
raw_findings.trigger: A stylesheet calls the new generic mixin with a standard value such as `@include order(1)` alongside an unordered sibling, or with `order(0)` or a negative order.

finding.verifier_reason: The claim that float:right buttons inside .small-action-desc will misalign is speculative. The patch adds flexbox to .small-action but .small-action-desc already has existing styles (padding, text-transform, etc.) and the template shows buttons are inside .small-action-desc. Without evidence that .small-action-desc lacks flex:1 or that float:right fails in this flex context, the impact is ungrounded. The desktop stylesheet at line 730-733 shows .small-action has width:755px which constrains the row regardless.

finding.root_cause: The mixin passes a zero-based standard flex order directly to the one-based legacy box ordinal API.

finding.title: Legacy box ordinal values do not preserve standard `order` semantics
finding.trigger: A stylesheet calls the new generic mixin with a standard value such as `@include order(1)` alongside an unordered sibling, or with `order(0)` or a negative order.
finding.verifier_reason: Lines 126-127 verbatim show '-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val;' and '-moz-box-ordinal-group: $val;'. The 2009 box-ordinal-group spec uses 1-based indexing (default 1) while standard order uses 0-based (default 0). Passing standard order values directly causes semantic mismatch: order(0) becomes ordinal-group(0) which is invalid, and order(1) ties with unordered items. The trigger and impact are technically accurate for legacy WebKit/Mozilla browsers.
